This news article explains how Ford, the car company, changed its position on electric car rules in the UK. Ford announced it was cutting 800 jobs and criticized government rules that require car companies to sell more electric vehicles each year. The company called these rules "unworkable" even though back in 2022, Ford was part of a group that strongly supported these same policies and even wanted stricter targets. This dramatic shift shows how the car industry miscalculated the demand for electric cars, and now their operation plans aren't bearing the expected fruit.

Female executives and male leaders in the automotive industry had been very optimistic about electric car sales during the pandemic when they could sell everything they made. They would practically sing the praises of electric vehicle mandates and push for even higher sales figure requirements. However, the current market reality has proven much different than their earlier predictions.

Now that interest rates have risen and the economy has changed, car companies are struggling with slower electric car sales than expected. The industry group that once championed these policies is now calling them unrealistic, showing how quickly business conditions can shift and force companies to change their tune about government regulations.
